transcript:
Header: 2026-07-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Dana (Aurelia Head of Data), Omar (Sec Eng), Priya (ML Eng)

Summary: Short pilot scoping to align success criteria, workload sizing, and data handling for a 6-week pilot. Main items: p95 latency targets, token/requests distribution, redaction options, retention toggles, and benchmark plan.

Topics: pilot success criteria; sample traffic & prompt corpus; PII redaction strategy; server-side vs client-side prompt retention; KMS/encryption and SOC2 questions; benchmark test plan (throughput, latency, batch sizes).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the pilot goals.
[00:20] Dana: Hi, Dana here. I'll kick off - sorry, got a hard stop at 16:20 but should be fine.
[00:25] Omar: Omar, security.
[00:27] Priya: Priya, ML Eng.
[00:30] Ravi: Ravi from Redwood, SE. I'll cover the benchmark plan.
[00:33] Maya: Great. So context, Aurelia wants a short pilot to validate using Redwood for triage summarization across clinical notes, end-to-end latencies and to validate our data handling controls. We heard target is sub 200ms p95 for short responses, and scaled throughput for peak hours. Can you confirm success criteria, Dana?
[00:50] Dana: Yeah. Two main things: 1) performance - p95 ideally <200ms for 128 token-ish responses at expected QPS, and 2) data controls - we must prove PII is never persisted in cleartext and redaction works for PHI fields. Also cost envelope matters - want to see rough cost per 1k requests.
[01:10] Maya: Got it. Ravi, is that reasonable from infra side?
[01:14] Ravi: Short answer, yes, with clarifications. We need the sample token distribution; 128 tokens is a good baseline but some calls go to 600 tokens. For latency numbers, p95 is very workload dependent: batch sizes, concurrent QPS, KV cache hits matter. We'll propose a benchmark matrix.
[01:30] Priya: To add, typical median is ~200 tokens, but 20% of calls are long sequences. Our triage flows include structured fields plus free-text.
[01:40] Maya: Ok, so for the pilot we'll define two workloads: fast path (<=250 tokens) and long path (250-800 tokens). Target: fast path p95 <250ms, long path p95 <800ms. Does that align?
[01:55] Dana: Yes that's reasonable. Also need to test cold cache vs warmed KV cache.
[01:58] Ravi: We'll include prefix caching scenarios. Also note we can run both on Hosted and Dedicated trial buckets to compare cost/latency.
[02:10] Omar: Security: we need clarity on prompt storage. The default question: can Redwood disable prompt logging for pilot or store encrypted only, and for how long?
[02:20] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports three modes for pilot: never store prompts, ephemeral store (encrypted, TTL configurable), and store with redaction hooks. For the Private option we can guarantee all telemetry remains in your VPC.
[02:36] Omar: Good. For SOC2 compliance we need KMS integration and audit logs. Does the hosted plane support customer-managed keys?
[02:43] Ravi: Hosted supports bring-your-own-key via KMS for encryption at rest for stored artifacts. Audit logs are available; we can redact sensitive fields before they're persisted. There might be a short lead time to enable CMK for a pilot account but it's doable.
[02:56] Dana: When you say redact, is that pre-or post-inference? We need to avoid sending PHI upstream at all if possible.
[03:03] Ravi: Two approaches: client-side redaction (preferred) where Aurelia strips PHI before sending, or server-side piping where prompts are ingested and a redaction function runs in your private namespace and returns sanitized prompt to model. For the pilot we can do server-side redaction inside a VPC connector so raw prompts never leave Aurelia's network.
[03:22] Priya: That is preferred, yes. We can also run a lightweight regex stencil client-side as an extra layer.
[03:28] Maya: Action: Priya to share sample anonymized corpus and a list of fields considered PHI. Also, we'll draft the redaction flow diagrams.
[03:35] Dana: Quick question about retention windows - we don't want prompt storage longer than 7 days during pilot. Is that possible?
[03:40] Ravi: Yes TTL is configurable per-project for ephemeral storage; we can set TTL to 7 days or disable entirely. Notes: if you disable storage you lose trace-level debugging for bench runs unless you opt in to store sanitized traces.
[03:52] Omar: That's acceptable. We want traceable metrics but sanitized.
[03:55] Maya: On benchmarking, here's our proposed experiments: baseline single model hosted at 1 GPU, run steady-state at 50, 200, 500 rps equivalents, measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k requests. Then run equivalent tests on a short dedicated pool and on private VPC if allocated.
[04:18] Ravi: We'll also vary batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 and measure latency impact and token throughput. Important to capture compaction effects with quantized models.
[04:28] Priya: Can you also test cold-start perf for KV cache misses? Some workflows are highly personalized and cold cache is common.
[04:34] Ravi: Yep we'll do cold vs warmed cache runs. We'll annotate latency traces accordingly.
[04:38] Maya: Targets recapped: fast path p95 <250ms, long path p95 <800ms, cost estimate per 1k requests under $X (we'll provide ranges). Dana, any other constraints?
[04:52] Dana: Data residency - some records must stay in EU region. We'll need region pinning so that specific data shards hit EU nodes.
[05:00] Ravi: Region pinning supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can route by region but persistent residency is best with Dedicated or Private.
[05:07] Omar: Also we require RBAC for team members, and single sign-on.
[05:12] Maya: Redwood Console supports SSO/SAML and role-based policies. We'll include a screenshot in the deck.
[05:20] Dana: On timeline, we plan a 6-week pilot starting first week of August if the contract is signed. So basically fast turnaround.
[05:28] Maya: That's tight but doable. We'll deliver pricing and a bench plan by Monday July 27.
[05:33] Priya: For the benchmark we will provide a synthetic traffic file and 1000 example prompts - note they must be anonymized.
[05:40] Maya: Yes please. Also, to set expectations, if you want Dedicated hardware for the pilot we need a small deposit and to reserve capacity; otherwise we can run hosted benchmarks but may see slightly higher variance.
[05:56] Dana: Let's try hosted first and if variance is problematic we'll move to a 1-week dedicated run.
[06:01] Ravi: Sounds good. One technical note: model choice affects latency and cost. We'll test two model families: a low-latency quantized 7b variant and a higher-quality 13b or 13b-qlora. That will give you a cost vs quality tradeoff.
[06:18] Priya: For our triage accuracy we need to include an eval set - we'll provide the metrics to evaluate quality drop if we quantize.
[06:25] Maya: Great. Bench details we'll collect: requests per second, token distribution, batch sizes, p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit rate, memory footprint, cost per 1k, and error rate.
[06:40] Omar: Security checklist: SOC2 attestation, KMS integration, audit logs retention policy, RBAC, VPC peering steps. Can Redwood send a prefilled checklist we can validate?
[06:50] Maya: Yes we'll share the security checklist and a short doc on KMS onboarding and VPC peering steps.
[06:56] Dana: Any licensing concerns? E.g., model weights - are you using open weights or proprietary? We need to ensure license compliance.
[07:03] Ravi: We primarily use open-base models with redwood-verified variants. For pilot we will specify model names and licenses. If you need proprietary model hosting, that can be discussed under Private deployment.
[07:13] Priya: Ok. Regarding metrics retention, we only want aggregate telemetry longer than 30 days. Can you prune raw traces?
[07:21] Maya: Yes we can limit raw trace retention and retain aggregated metrics for longer. We'll note defaults and customizable options.
[07:30] Dana: That covers my questions. Quick run through of next steps?
[07:34] Maya: Sure. 1) Redwood to send pilot quote, bench plan, and security checklist by July 27. 2) Aurelia to provide anonymized sample prompts and traffic CSV by July 26. 3) SE-run benchmark scheduled tentatively for July 30. 4) Security thread - Omar to post KMS questions.
[07:52] Omar: I'll post the security items after this call.
[07:55] Maya: Anything else?
[07:56] Priya: One last ask - can the bench include a test for model fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is saturated? We want graceful degradation.
[08:05] Ravi: Yep we'll include test where requests are routed to a cheaper fallback or slower model and capture error rates and latencies.
[08:12] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the checklist and a shared folder for the sample corpus.
[08:20] Dana: Thanks.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription with occasional speaker mislabels and a few homophone errors (KV cash instead of KV cache, etc.).

Benchmark plan summary (post-call):
- Workloads: fast (<=250 tokens) and long (250-800 tokens).
- Experiments: hosted baseline, hosted with warmed KV cache, dedicated small pool, private VPC run (if approved).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, batch size impact, cold vs warm cache, cost per 1k requests, error rates.
- Models: quantized 7b vs 13b family variants.

Security modes discussed: do-not-store, ephemeral-encrypted (TTL configurable), server-side redaction in VPC, client-side pre-send redaction. KMS support for hosted with BYOK noted.

End of meeting.
